column12: Lightest quark. Two of them plus a down quark make a proton.
Partner of the up quark. Two downs and an up make a neutron.
Heavier copy of the up quark; its discovery confirmed the quark model.
Named for the strangely long lifetime of the particles containing it.
Heaviest known particle, as massive as a gold atom. Decays before it can bind.
Long-lived enough to leave a measurable track; the workhorse of flavour physics.
Carries electricity, holds atoms together, does all of chemistry.
Almost massless, almost never interacts. Trillions pass through you each second.
A heavy electron that lives 2.2 microseconds. \"Who ordered that?\"
Proved neutrinos come in distinct flavours.
Heavy enough to decay into hadrons, unlike its lighter cousins.
The last fermion of the Standard Model to be observed directly.
Carries electromagnetism. Massless, so its reach is unlimited.
Carries the strong force. Carries color itself, so gluons pull on each other.
Carries the weak force and changes one flavour into another. Beta decay is its work.
The neutral weak carrier. Heavy, so the weak force barely reaches past a nucleus.
A ripple in the field that gives the other particles their mass.
Two up quarks and a down, bound by gluons. Its count is the atomic number.
Two down quarks and an up. Free ones decay in about 15 minutes.
